the_signal.headline: Prompt testing frameworks now catch AI workflow regressions before production
the_signal.body: n8n's systematic prompt testing approach treats LLM behavior like code: validate outputs, catch drift, prevent silent failures in revenue workflows. For GTM teams running AI-powered qualification or lead scoring, untested prompt changes are invisible revenue leaks. This shifts AI automation from 'hope it works' to 'prove it works'.

thread_of_day.title: Why Developers Avoid Platform Tools (and What GTM Teams Should Learn)
thread_of_day.takeaway: Developers choose flexibility and control over convenience — the same principle applies to GTM engineers choosing between iPaaS, API management, and custom orchestration.

quote.text: iPaaS versus API management tools: engineering teams that need execution control, self-hosting, and code-level extensibility reach for n8n.
quote.source: n8n Blog: iPaaS vs. API Management

whats_moving.context: Model routing, caching, and parallel execution are moving from 'nice to have' to required patterns as AI workflows scale into production revenue systems.
The transactional outbox pattern is gaining traction for guaranteeing webhook and event delivery in workflows that touch customer data or revenue transactions.
n8n's new Agent paradigm (describe → deploy) is lowering the barrier for non-engineers to build executable automations, expanding GTM team self-service.

act_on_this: Audit one production AI workflow for prompt drift: run your current prompt against 10 historical edge-case inputs and compare outputs to your baseline. Document what changes.

numbers.stat: Transactional outbox pattern prevents dual-write failures in event-driven systems
numbers.context: For GTM workflows publishing leads to CRM + analytics simultaneously, this pattern eliminates the 'lost event' scenarios that tank reconciliation and skew pipeline reporting.
